paper.title: Fine-Grained Vehicle Make and Model Recognition Framework Based on Magnetic Fingerprint

evidence.paraphrase: The study directly classifies 36 vehicle makes/models in a traffic setting, so its machine group is substantively correct.
Recognition uses magnetic-field fingerprints from roadside sensors explicitly instead of surveillance-camera video, with no semantic-part or temporal video fusion method.
The supplied publication year is 2024, later than the supplied 2023 cutoff.

reviews.rationale: The paper directly studies fine-grained vehicle make/model recognition and therefore fits the assigned evidence group. It is nevertheless outside this video's method scope because the abstract explicitly replaces surveillance video with magnetic sensor data; it also postdates the supplied cutoff.

paper.title: RESEARCH ON MULTI-OBJECT TRACKING OF PIGS BASED ON IMPROVED BYTE TRACK

evidence.paraphrase: The target population is pigs rather than vehicles.
YOLOv8 and an improved ByteTrack pipeline address occlusion-related trajectory interruption, so the method is only a cross-domain tracking analogue.
The supplied publication year is 2026, later than the supplied 2023 cutoff.

reviews.rationale: The abstract concerns livestock tracking for pig-farm behavior and activity applications, not vehicle make recognition or a vehicle detection/tracking pipeline. Its occlusion-aware multi-object tracking method is a partial methodological analogue, but that does not overcome the wrong population and post-cutoff year.

paper.title: Vehicle Classification Algorithm Based on Improved Vision Transformer

evidence.paraphrase: The model extracts local features and uses sparse attention to select discernible image regions, giving a limited analogue to local-region evidence.

The reported task is generic vehicle classification on BIT-Vehicles plus three non-vehicle image datasets; the abstract does not identify semantic vehicle parts, occlusion testing, make/model classes, or video aggregation.
The supplied publication year is 2024, later than the supplied 2023 cutoff.

reviews.rationale: Local-feature extraction and attention make this a partial analogue for region-based evidence, but the abstract supports only generic image classification rather than semantic vehicle parts under occlusion or video-based make recognition. The evidence is sufficient to exclude it from the narrow scope, and the supplied year is also beyond the cutoff.

paper.title: Exploring Multi-Modal Spatial–Temporal Contexts for High-Performance RGB-T Tracking

evidence.paraphrase: A quality-aware decoder propagates tracking cues from historical frames to the current frame, making the study a bridge for temporal evidence handling.

The outcome is generic RGB-thermal object tracking on RGB-T benchmarks, with no vehicle population, make/model classification, semantic vehicle parts, or branch-first versus frame-first fusion comparison.
The supplied publication year is 2024, later than the supplied 2023 cutoff.

reviews.rationale: The temporal propagation and quality-aware components provide a legitimate methodological bridge to multi-frame evidence fusion. However, the abstract evaluates generic RGB-T tracking rather than vehicle make recognition, so it is only a partial group analogue and lies outside the research scope; it also postdates the cutoff.
